newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Swire says may buy back more shares.
newsitem.headline: Swire says may buy back more shares.

text.p: Swire Pacific Ltd's share price did not reflect its sound fundamentals, and the company may buy back more shares if that will add shareholder value, Swire Pacific chairman Peter Sutch said on Thursday.
The blue chip conglomerate bought back 8.15 million of its A-shares and 7.70 million of its B-shares in the first quarter of the year, a company spokswoman said.
When asked if Swire Pacific would buy back more shares, Sutch told a news conference: "If we considered this to be (in) the interest of the shareholders, yes."
"We don't have a formal plan to buy that 'X' percent," said Peter Johansen, Swire Pacific's group finance director, adding that it depended on the shares' performance.
Sutch said the company was disappointed by its shares' performance, saying it did not reflect business fundamentals.
The stock has fallen 16 percent so far this year, from HK$73.75 on December 31 to HK$61.50 on Thursday, while the Hang Seng Index has risen about 4.4 percent in the same period.
Sutch said the share price might reflect a suspicion that Swire Pacific was not enthusiastic about replenishing its land bank. "I hope we put that one to rest," he said.
